data.title: Why SpaceX stock is down around 3% on Tuesday
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock slipped nearly 3% early Tuesday, extending a roughly 2% decline on Monday.

Shares were trading around $144, close to the level of their $150 debut price.

The stock has nevertheless recovered significantly over the past several weeks after falling to a record low of $104.83 on August 3.

The latest pullback comes as investors look ahead to both additional lockup releases and a potentially important Starship test later this month.

SpaceX faces billions in upcoming unlocks

Unlike a typical IPO, SpaceX did not establish a single 180-day lockup expiration.

Its prospectus instead spread insider selling eligibility across roughly a dozen dates, limiting the amount of new supply released at any one time.

The staggered structure, however, has not eliminated the pressure from potential selling.

Shares fell around 3% during the latest major release after up to 319 million Class A shares became eligible for trading, representing roughly $49 billion at recent prices.

Another 59.1 million affiliate shares became unlocked the following day.

Several additional unlocks are scheduled before the end of 2026.

On September 24, around 320 million shares are expected to become eligible for trading.

Another roughly 320 million shares are scheduled for October 9 and October 24.

The largest release is expected two full trading days after SpaceX reports third-quarter results, which are expected in late October or early November.

Up to 1.3 billion shares, or about 28% of the relevant share pool, could become sellable at that point.

December 8 marks the 180-day expiration, when the remaining non-Musk insider float becomes eligible.

By the end of 2026, roughly 4.9 billion SpaceX shares are expected to have become available for trading.

That creates a persistent overhang for investors, particularly as early shareholders gain more opportunities to take profits following SpaceX’s recovery from its August low.

Starship Flight 14 approaches

While the lockup schedule represents a supply-side risk for SPCX, Starship remains one of the company’s biggest potential long-term catalysts.

SpaceX is scheduled to launch its 14th Starship test flight on September 22 from Starbase, Texas, according to the FAA’s Current Operations Plan Advisory.

September 23 is listed as a backup date.

The launch comes after CFO Bret Johnsen said last week that Flight 14 will be the first revenue-generating flight for Starship.

The spacecraft is expected to carry production-grade Version 3 Starlink satellites into orbit, which Johnsen described as a major milestone.

Elon Musk said Monday that Flight 14 will be the final test before SpaceX attempts to catch the Starship spacecraft with its launch tower.

“We've got flight 14 coming up, of Starship, and this will be the last flight before we attempt to catch the ship,” Musk said at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles. “So if this flight goes well, then on flight 15 we will try to catch the ship.”

Musk also said SpaceX could later this year, or more likely early next year, attempt to refly both the Starship spacecraft and booster.

SpaceX has already demonstrated the ability to reuse its boosters, but it has yet to successfully perform a tower catch of the Starship spacecraft or fly the ship again.

Starship is central to the valuation

The upcoming tests matter because a large part of SpaceX’s long-term growth potential depends on turning Starship into a reusable, high-frequency launch system.

Pivotal Research Group analyst Jeffrey Wlodarczak said earlier this month that achieving full reusability is central to whether SpaceX’s roughly $2 trillion valuation can be justified.

His $220 price target assumes Starship can achieve 20 to 50 flights per vehicle, low refurbishment costs and rapid turnaround times.

“Our $220 target is a call on reuse of 20-50 flights per vehicle, cheap refurb, fast turnaround,” Wlodarczak said. “If that is solved, the rest of the model can happen. If it is not, SPCX is a different and much smaller company.”

The potential scale is significant. SpaceX says Starship can carry more than 100 metric tons of payload, more than four times the capacity of its Falcon 9.

data.title: Tilray stock has slumped 55% this year: is it a golden opportunity to buy?
data.description:
Tilray Brands stock has remained under pressure and is underperforming the market this year. TLRY was trading at $4.15 after falling by 55% since January and by 62% in the last 12 months. Still, a contrarian case can be made despite its ongoing challenges. 

Tilray Brands is doing fairly well despite challenges

The cannabis industry is going through a tough situation, with demand falling, competition rising, and the rescheduling taking longer than expected. 

Tilray Brands’ business has been affected by these developments. Nonetheless, a closer look at its recent results shows that its business is doing relatively well. 

The most recent results shows that its annual revenue rose by 11% to $915 million in the last financial year. It rose by 25% in the fourth quarter to $281 million, partly because of its acquisitions.

Its cannabis revenue rose by 5% to $71.5 million, with its gross margin remaining unchanged at 44%. The beverage business generated $105 million in revenue, up sharply from the $65.6 million it made last year. Also, its annual revenue rose by 6% to over $254 million. 

The distribution revenue rose by 15% to $85 million, while the smaller wellness revenue rose by 16% to $19.7 million. These numbers mean that the company is seeing modest growth across the board, which the management has pledged to accelerate. 

The company also narrowed its losses during the quarter. It reported a non-cash loss of $37.9 million, mostly because of non-cash charges. 

Analysts are optimistic that Tilray Brands' revenue will continue growing in the foreseeable future. The average estimate among analysts is that its annual revenue will rise by 22% to $1.12 billion. It will then hit $1.18 billion next year. In most cases, Tilray Brands tends to outperform its top-line numbers, meaning that its real figures will be better than expected.

Another potential catalyst is the rescheduling of cannabis. Tilray does not have cannabis operations in the US, meaning that it may enter the country once the rescheduling process ends. The company said:

“Following recent U.S. rescheduling developments, Tilray continues to evaluate multiple pathways to participation in an emerging federally compliant, science-driven medical cannabis market.”

Tilray stock price technical analysis

TLRY stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the TLRY stock has been in a strong sell-off since last year. It has formed a descending channel and remained below all moving average indicators. 

The stock is hovering near the key support level of $3.69, which is part of a double-bottom pattern whose neckline is at $4.95. Therefore, the stock will likely retreat to the key support of $3.70 and then bounce back. 

If this happens, the initial target will be at $4.95. A move above that level will point to more gains, potentially to $5. This view will remain as long as it is above the double-bottom of $3.70.

data.title: Crypto stocks slide as Bitcoin drops ahead of Clarity Act vote and Fed decision
data.description:
Crypto-linked stocks fell sharply Tuesday morning as Bitcoin declined and investors awaited a critical Senate vote on crypto regulation, with the Federal Reserve’s rate decision also due Wednesday.

Coinbase Global shares fell 7% to $178.

Strategy, formerly known as MicroStrategy, slid 5% to $130.32.

MARA Holdings dropped a more modest 2% to $11.2.

Bitcoin was down 3.1% over the past 24 hours, trading at $76,180.

The Senate vote is the day’s key catalyst

The Senate is scheduled to vote at 2:15 PM ET on whether to advance the Clarity Act, legislation intended to create a clearer federal framework for digital assets.

The bill needs 60 votes to clear the procedural hurdle, and its path remains uncertain given continued political disagreement.

Even if the vote passes, it would not enact the bill into law; it would only allow the legislation to advance in the Senate.

A failed vote could leave the industry’s regulatory questions unresolved for longer.

Why the stocks are falling harder than Bitcoin itself

The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, which tracks Bitcoin directly, fell 3% to $43.19, roughly in line with Bitcoin’s own decline.

But Strategy and Coinbase fell by wider margins, 5% and 7% respectively, than Bitcoin’s 3% drop.

Strategy’s business is built around its large Bitcoin holdings, which tends to amplify the stock’s moves relative to Bitcoin’s own price swings.

MARA Holdings also carries Bitcoin exposure through its mining operations and holdings, though its decline was more contained than Coinbase’s or Strategy’s.

The broader market fared better as the S&P 500 index fell only 0.5%, showing that crypto-linked names witnessed a stronger bout of selling. 

Ark Invest trims Coinbase

Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest sold shares of Coinbase, Circle Internet Group, Bullish, Bitmine Immersion Technologies and its own spot Bitcoin ETF on Monday, as crypto-related stocks advanced.

According to the firm’s latest trade disclosure, Ark Invest sold 36,628 Coinbase (COIN) shares, worth about $7 million based on Monday’s closing price of $191.45. Coinbase shares gained 9.24% during the session.

Ark Invest also sold 142,350 shares of Circle Internet Group (CRCL) across two funds, valued at roughly $13.8 million. Circle shares closed 7.53% higher at $97.42.

What comes next

Coinbase, as one of the largest US cryptocurrency exchanges, stands to benefit most directly from a clearer regulatory framework, which could support more institutional participation in the sector.

Investors are now watching two things over the next two days: whether the Senate advances the Clarity Act this afternoon, and how the Federal Reserve’s rate decision Wednesday affects broader risk appetite.

Both outcomes are likely to move crypto-linked stocks more than the market overall.

Analysts framed Tuesday’s selloff as a near-term reaction rather than a verdict on crypto’s longer-term outlook.

If the Clarity Act eventually clears Congress and Bitcoin stabilizes, Coinbase, Strategy and MARA could all benefit from clearer rules and renewed institutional interest.

Investors holding crypto-linked stocks are generally advised to keep position sizes moderate given that volatility, rather than treat today’s price action as a signal to go all in either way.

data.title: Bank of America stock in focus after CEO warns of slower Q3 revenue growth
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) shares were in focus on Tuesday after the financial services firm issued disappointing guidance for its fiscal Q3.

Speaking at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference, CEO Brian Moynihan said BAC’s investment banking fees and trading revenue will fall notably short of the solid growth seen earlier this year.

Bank of America stock was up 0.13% at the time of writing. However, the stock is down some 8% versus its recent high.

Bank of America’s Q3 guidance signals a slowdown

BAC shares are in focus because of a downward revision in core revenue drivers.

Moynihan cautioned investors that Q3 investment banking fees are expected to decline by as much as 20% on a year-over-year basis, tracking between $1.6 billion and $1.8 billion.

Compounding this pressure is the bank’s sales and trading unit, with the chief executive projecting trading revenue to remain roughly flat versus the same period last year.

While the Bank of America observed marginal growth in its equities trading segment this quarter, its fixed-income division faced unexpected volatility and declines.

Together, these figures fall short of analysts’ expectations – indicating the lucrative capital markets environment may be cooling faster than Wall Street anticipated.

Broader industry facing headwinds in late 2026

Bank of America’s guidance points to broader industry headwinds rather than isolated institutional failures, with CEO Brian Moynihan noting the overall investment banking market is down roughly 10% across the board.

The "higher-for-longer" interest rate environment continues to suppress deal-making pipelines and financing demand, squeezing advisory fees.

Note that BAC’s muted Q3 forecast represents a dramatic shift in momentum. Just a quarter earlier, the bank posted a remarkable 50% increase in investment banking fees and a 33% jump in trading revenue.

This rapid deceleration has investors questioning whether the recent capital markets boom is over already.

The stark contrast between the blistering first half of 2026 and the currently subdued fiscal Q3 has prompted a swift repricing of Bank of America shares.

How to play BAC shares at current levels?

The warning from Bank of America’s chief executive has triggered a ripple effect across the wider financial services sector, dragging down peers Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as well.

However, the long-term outlook for BAC stock isn't entirely bleak.

Despite the near-term capital market softness, Moynihan emphasized that the bank's deal pipeline remains robust, particularly within the middle-market sector.

From a valuation standpoint, Bank of America offers a sustainable dividend yield of about 2.15%, which continues to appeal to income-focused investors despite current price volatility.

The critical question for the upcoming earnings season is whether this Q3 slowdown is a temporary lull in deal timing or a more durable structural shift in the financial landscape.

Until that becomes clear, investors should brace for continued volatility.

data.title: Dow opens 250 points lower as oil prices and Treasury yields pressure stocks
data.description:
Major US stock indexes opened lower on Tuesday as rising crude prices, elevated Treasury yields and uncertainty over the outlook for artificial intelligence demand weighed on investor sentiment.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 253 points. The S&P 500 fell 0.23%, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.30%.

The cautious tone followed Monday’s selloff in technology stocks, which was driven partly by calls from leading artificial intelligence companies to slow the development of advanced AI models over safety concerns.

AI concerns keep technology stocks under pressure

Alphabet and Microsoft each fell about 1% in trading. Chipmakers, which suffered some of the sharpest losses during Monday’s session, traded in a narrower range on Tuesday.

On the otherhand, Nvidia shares rose around 1.12%, while other AI-linked stocks, including Advanced Micro Devices, Intel and Micron Technology, gained more than 1.6% in early trading.

The recent pressure followed calls from AI executives for a slower pace of model development.

However, the potential effect of such a slowdown on corporate spending and demand for computing infrastructure remains unclear.

The concerns have added to broader market uncertainty, with investors already dealing with above-target inflation and the prospect of higher borrowing costs.

Shares of Dave & Buster’s Entertainment fell more than 7% after the arcade and entertainment chain reported second-quarter revenue below expectations.

Meanwhile, Waystar shares climbed 6.7% after reports said that the healthcare software company was exploring strategic options, including a potential sale.

Oil prices and Treasury yields raise inflation concerns

Oil prices continued to rise as the conflict in the Middle East showed few signs of easing. Brent crude futures increased 0.6% to $106.31 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures rose 1.2% to $102.59.

Crude prices extended gains after Saudi Arabia shut a key pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

The increase in energy prices has intensified concerns that a supply shock could push inflation higher.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note also reached 5.041%, its highest level since 2007, before easing slightly. It was later around 4.996%.

Higher Treasury yields can reduce the relative appeal of equities by increasing the return available from lower-risk government debt.

Rising yields can also place pressure on stock valuations, particularly in sectors whose expected earnings are further in the future.

Fed rate decision remains central to investor focus

Markets are preparing for the Federal Reserve’s policy decision on Wednesday.

Fed funds futures indicated a roughly 92% probability of a quarter-point rate increase from the current target range of 3.5% to 3.75%.

Recent economic data have provided limited relief for investors. Consumer prices accelerated in August, while a measure of underlying inflation recorded its largest increase in four months.

Barclays strategists said higher interest rates had already pressured equity valuations.

They warned that a sustained move above the 5% level for 10-year Treasury yields could become a more persistent headwind for stocks.

The strategists maintained a constructive base case for equities because of continued earnings momentum but cautioned that the risk of a sharper market repricing would increase if yields moved materially higher.

data.title: Why is Cardano price falling despite the x402 integration?
data.description:
ADA has fallen roughly 3% over the past 24 hours to trade near $0.204 on Sept. 15, extending its seven-day loss despite Cardano’s recent integration with the x402 payment standard.

CoinGecko puts ADA at roughly $0.204, down more than 7% over the past week, after the token traded above $0.22 on Sept. 9 and briefly recovered towards $0.214 earlier on Monday. 

The latest rebound was quickly sold, leaving the token just above the $0.20 level.

Cardano’s x402 integration has failed to reverse the decline so far. 

The payment standard uses the HTTP 402 protocol to let software, including autonomous AI agents, make machine-to-machine payments without conventional accounts or checkout systems, giving Cardano developers another way to build automated payment applications.

The integration, however, does not require users or developers to immediately buy large amounts of ADA. 

Its effect on the token would depend on applications adopting x402 on Cardano, transaction activity increasing, and ADA capturing demand generated by those applications.

Price action over the past week shows that buying has remained weak despite the announcement. 

ADA started the period above $0.22, fell towards $0.205 by Sept. 11 and spent much of the following sessions struggling below $0.21. 

Monday’s rebound towards $0.214 was rejected before the token returned to roughly $0.204.

The decline extends a pattern that has developed since late August. 

ADA traded above $0.24 and briefly moved considerably higher around Aug. 22, but sellers pushed it back towards $0.20. 

Another recovery in early September stalled around $0.23, leaving successive rebounds below the August peak.

Pressure across the crypto market has made those recoveries harder to sustain. 

Bitcoin has slipped below the $77,000-$77,500 region while traders face uncertainty around the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and the US Senate’s CLARITY Act proceedings.

US Treasury yields have climbed as oil prices above $100 renewed inflation concerns, creating a difficult backdrop for risk assets.

ADA’s recent derivatives positioning has created another source of pressure. 

Long-heavy positioning leaves leveraged traders exposed when the spot price falls, as liquidations can force positions to close during a decline and increase short-term selling.

ADA price analysis

ADA’s daily chart keeps the larger downtrend intact despite its recovery from the June low near $0.145. 

Price climbed as high as roughly $0.245 in August but failed to regain the large volume area around $0.245-$0.25, where the Volume Profile shows one of the strongest concentrations of historical trading activity.

The Volume Profile places another large trading cluster around $0.17-$0.18. With ADA now near $0.204, price is sitting between those two major volume zones. 

A break below $0.20 would leave the $0.18 area as the first notable downside target, followed by the high-volume region around $0.17. 

Losing that area could expose the June zone near $0.145-$0.15.

Aroon readings on the daily chart favour sellers. Aroon Down stands near 50%, while Aroon Up has dropped to roughly 7.1%. 

The low Aroon Up reading shows that ADA has not made a recent high strong enough to establish an active upward trend. 

A move back above $0.22 would begin to change the recent price structure, while the larger resistance zone remains around $0.24-$0.25.

On the 4-hour chart, ADA is trading near $0.2046 and remains below the Supertrend resistance at roughly $0.2167. See below.

Price briefly pushed above $0.21 during the latest rebound but could not hold the move, keeping the Supertrend bearish. 

ADA would need to reclaim $0.2167 and then clear the recent $0.22-$0.23 highs before $0.24-$0.25 comes back into range.

Chaikin Money Flow has fallen to roughly -0.21 on the 4-hour chart, moving further below zero as ADA returned towards $0.20. 

The negative reading shows that selling pressure has outweighed buying pressure across the indicator’s lookback period. 

A recovery above zero alongside a move through $0.2167 would provide stronger confirmation that buyers are returning.

For the downside, $0.20 remains the immediate level to watch. A clean break below it would expose roughly $0.19 before the $0.17-$0.18 volume cluster. 

Holding $0.20 and reclaiming the 4-hour Supertrend near $0.2167 would instead put $0.23 in view, followed by the much stronger $0.24-$0.25 resistance area.

data.title: Meta stock outlook: can Muse AI and legal relief push shares above $700?
data.description:
Meta Platforms’ stock META has been caught between enthusiasm over its artificial intelligence ambitions and concerns about the enormous cost of funding those efforts.

The latest rebound is giving bulls fresh reason to believe the company could finally be approaching a sustained breakout, Bloomberg reported, although analysts remain divided over whether the rally can last.

Meta shares have risen 22% from their August low and are on track for their strongest monthly gain since May 2025.

The recovery accelerated after the company settled a major social-media lawsuit and introduced Muse, an AI agent designed to automate everyday tasks for consumers.

The developments have helped revive the investment case for Meta after a year of repeated rallies that ultimately failed to hold.

Meta stock has already experienced four trough-to-peak gains of at least 20% in 2026.

Each rally subsequently faded, with the stock recording lower highs along the way.

That has left the shares essentially flat for the year, compared with a roughly 15% gain for the Nasdaq 100.

Meta was up about 1.4% today, touching $675.

Bulls see catalysts for a breakout

Investors betting on a sustained recovery believe the latest combination of legal relief and AI product momentum could be different.

"Eliminating a legal overhang and then having a positive product in a hot narrative is certainly enough to get the early stages of a trend change going," Dan Russo, co-chief investment officer at Potomac Fund Management, which owns Meta shares, said in the Bloomberg report.

"We've seen a number of these counter-trend rallies fizzle out and fade. What's key from here is to build on the momentum and validate the changing trend."

For Russo, that validation would require Meta stock to break decisively above $700 and remain there.

The $18 billion settlement of Meta's social-media lawsuit has also removed a significant source of uncertainty.

The company had previously calculated that an adverse trial outcome could have exposed it to penalties of as much as $1.4 trillion.

Meta shares have fallen in only four of the 12 trading sessions since the settlement was announced on Aug. 26.

AI products strengthen the investment case

The legal resolution has arrived alongside renewed optimism about Meta’s AI ambitions.

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak compared Meta’s current setup with Alphabet’s position in late 2025, when the Google parent received a favourable ruling in a long-running antitrust case and subsequently launched a series of AI products.

Alphabet shares have since gained more than 50%, becoming the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock over that period.

Nowak believes Meta could similarly benefit as it continues to roll out AI products.

Meta is in position to keep releasing new products, "which in aggregate could add $10+ to EPS," Nowak wrote in an Aug. 30 note.

"We don't believe these are priced in Meta right now," he added, arguing that the stock is trading below its valuation peak in 2025, when investors viewed Meta as an "AI winner" and GPU investments were helping drive faster growth.

JPMorgan has also become more positive, upgrading Meta to overweight last week.

Analyst Doug Anmuth cited "strong early traction" for Muse and said the product demonstrated why Meta could have an advantage in bringing consumer-focused AI products to its enormous user base.

"Meta is well-positioned to deliver consumer-driven AI products to its base of about 4B users," Anmuth said.

"There's still meaningful upside potential as Meta is in the early stages of releasing frontier models and AI-driven products beyond advertising," he added.

Cheap valuation comes with a big spending risk

Meta’s valuation could provide another reason for investors to consider the stock after its recent weakness.

The company trades at roughly 18 times estimated earnings for the next 12 months, below its 10-year average of about 20 times and more than 30% below its 2025 peak.

At the same time, analysts expect revenue to grow by more than 25% this year, while earnings are forecast to increase by more than 30%.

But the stock’s relatively inexpensive valuation also reflects concerns about the enormous investment required to compete in AI.

Meta's capital expenditure is expected to nearly double to about $140 billion this year and rise to almost $200 billion in 2027.

That spending is expected to put substantial pressure on free cash flow.

After previously generating significant cash flows, Meta is projected to post negative free cash flow of about $6.3 billion this year, with the deficit potentially widening to almost $30 billion in 2027.

Investors remain divided over the rally

Those spending requirements are keeping some investors from fully embracing Meta’s recovery.

Cyrus Amini, chief investment officer at Hyphen Wealth Management, said the stock’s valuation and near-term catalysts were attractive, but questioned whether those factors were enough to support a longer-term rally.

"The valuation is attractive, and it could have more short-term catalysts than megacaps, but for anything beyond that, all bets are off. It could easily fade again," he said in the Bloomberg report.

"Things are changing so fast it's hard to safely say any name is a long-term winner."

data.title: Why Joby Aviation stock is falling as it nears a major inflection point
data.description:
Joby Aviation stock remains in a freefall this week and is hovering at its lowest level since May 2025. It slipped to $6.30, down more than 70% from its high last year, with its valuation falling from over $17.4 billion to $6.2 billion today. This retreat may continue, even as the company’s commercialization nears. 

Joby Aviation is at an inflection point

Joby Aviation is one of the top companies that seeks to disrupt the transportation industry. It has spent the last 17 years working on its electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft (eVTOL). 

In this period, it has spent billions of dollars researching and working on its flights. To achieve that, it has received substantial funding from companies like Baillie Gifford and Toyota. Toyota has now become a crucial shareholder with a 14.3% stake. 

The company has also raised capital through dilution. It has raised cash by selling shares in the past few years. As a result, the outstanding shares have jumped from 604 million in 2022 to 986 million today. 

Most importantly, Joby has used this period to seek FAA certification, which it will receive later this year. The company has also expanded its manufacturing process and is using Toyota’s track record in the industry. It has also made some notable customer deals, including with ANA and Virgin Atlantic.

At the same time, it is now expanding its presence in the defense industry. It is doing that by spending $500 million to acquire Resonant Sciences, which will now become its defense business. 

Resonant made over $100 million in revenue in the trailing twelve months and is growing by 40%. This matters because the US government plans to spend over $1.5 trillion on defense. 

READ MORE: Here’s why flying car stocks like Joby and Archer Aviation falling

The company plans to start its commercial events this year, and then scale it in the foreseeable future. Taken together, its commercialization and the ongoing pivot towards the defense industry mean that it is at an inflection point.

Analysts expect that its revenue, excluding Resonant, will continue growing, with its annual revenue rising to $125 million this year and $299 million next year.

Concerns about its business remains

Joby Aviation stock has slipped in the past few months as investors remain concerned about its business. This explains why it has a short interest of about 10%, a sign that investors expect it to continue its downward trend. 

One of the key concerns is that it will take a long time for the company to become profitable even when the commercialization process starts. This will see it continue raising capital, possibly through share sales. It recently announced a $750 million share sale to finance its Resonant business.

Joby Aviation stock technical analysis

JOBY Aviation chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that the JOBY share price has slumped in the past few years, falling from a record high of $21 to the current $6.30. It has formed a descending channel, a sign that bears remain in control.

The stock has dropped below the 78.6% Fibonacci Retracement level. It also fell below the 50-week and 100-week Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). Also, the Average Directional Index (ADX) has risen to 17.30 and is pointing upwards. 

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of $4.87, its lowest level in October 2024 and April last year.

data.title: XRP futures activity and changing market sentiment
data.description:
XRP futures markets draw the attention of traders. Futures trading, which has grown in significance, is a key component of digital asset analysis, and traders are increasingly looking at futures levels to gauge market sentiment and potential volatility.

XRP futures markets shed light on trader action, such as leverage use, longs and shorts, and risk appetite changes.

But heightening futures trading activity does not mean the price of XRP will rise or fall.

Participants in the market frequently compare the level of activity in derivatives markets involving the current price of XRP to the existing order-book activity in the spot market and determine whether this activity stems from hope and speculation or is indicative of a general demand for XRP.

Investors may trade the XRP futures contract based on their expectation of changes in the price of XRP in the future, as compared with spot trading, where an investor can purchase or sell some XRP at the current market rate.

This type of contract may also have leverage involved, meaning both winnings and losses can be greater.

Why futures activity matters for XRP

Why futures activity is so significant for XRP. Why futures trading is a key element for XRP.

Markets for futures contracts can affect short-term price fluctuations by enabling larger exposures through margin trading.

Traders can make a lot of money if they build their positions at the same time on the same side.

If they make their trades when lots of other traders have their trades on the same side with them, then markets can be more sensitive to changes in the price that they are seeing.

A strong reaction to trade in the direction of the positions can cause liquidations, further driving trade in the direction of the trades previously made.

  • Downtrends and lengthy Liquidations: when XRP is trading downwards, and lots of buyers have long leveraged trades, the positions can close because of a lack of enough margin. The following compelling income can place additional strain on the markets.
  • Uptrends and Short Liquidations: This is reversed during uptrends. Should numerous traders take a short position and XRP increases dramatically, short liquidations could compel them to exit their trades, which could produce momentum for the bull market.

It is important, therefore, to look at futures as a tool for gauging overall market positioning instead of a forecast of the likely direction of prices.

Open interest shows participation, not direction

Participation, not direction, is indicated by open interest.

Open interest is certainly one measure that is widely followed in the futures market.

It is the net long-to-short position of all the futures traders for a single commodity.

The higher the number of open interest, the more traders are active in XRP's derivatives market, but it does not show whether they think prices will rise or fall.

The open interest can be increased by:

  • New long traders coming into the market.
  • New short positions being created.
  • Raising capital leverage.
  • Increased involvement by retail or institutional investors.

Therefore, open interest is generally interpreted along with price changes, trading volume, funding rates, and the liquidity environment.

An increase in open interest with high buy and sell interest indicates wide market participation.

Higher leverage, however, alone, without solid puts and takes on the market, can induce extra volatility risks.

Leverage can increase market volatility

Leverage can make the market volatile. One of the primary reasons futures trading is more volatile than trading stocks is the effect it has on price.

Leverage allows the trader to trade on larger amounts, but with a relatively small amount of money.

This can lead to more exposure to potential benefits, but it also exposes the risks of getting taken under.

Under these two widely occurring situations, the system may either be:

  • Leveraged Long Trades: If there is a downward trend in the price of XRP, then the long trades might be forced to sell more of their assets, causing further downward pressure.
  • Short Liquidations: With rising prices, traders who are short on XRP may be required to cover their holdings with deals, leading to some upward pressure.

Thus, high futures activity is not necessarily a confident indication. It could also suggest a shift in the market to more extreme volatility.

Funding rates provide additional market context

Funding Sources: Additional market context. In addition, funding rates are a crucial futures metric, particularly in perpetual contracts.

They are important for maintaining futures prices in balance with spot market prices.

Typically, higher funding rates will reflect higher demand for a long position, whereas negative funding rates may suggest higher demand for a short position.

Funding rates aren't necessarily an official sign of the market, though. Overcrowded jobs have the potential to turn over more aggressively:

  • If the market is heavily long, it could be vulnerable to liquidation problems at the time of a market downturn.
  • If the market is heavily short, then it may be vulnerable to liquidation problems at the time of a market recovery.

Spot market activity remains important

Spot market activity continues to be significant. While the futures markets offer insight, there's also the activity on the spot market that needs to be taken into account when studying XRP conditions.

Derivatives data help to indicate traders' positioning, and spot markets help indicate buying and selling demand.

Wedge charts are commonly used by traders, and they look for specific patterns in the chart, along with key indicators such as:

  • Spot trading volume
  • Futures trading volume
  • Open interest
  • Funding rates
  • Global overall cryptocurrency market developments

Considering several indicators gives a more balanced view than considering only one indicator.

Understanding XRP Futures trading risks

To grasp the risks associated with trading XRP futures. To learn about the risks involved in futures trading.

Aside from the basic price investing strategy, there are other opportunities to take a position on XRP price movements on futures contracts, but those come with other risks compared to buying and holding the coins in a spot position.

Margin and leverage requirements in futures contracts, or liquidation policies, can make these types of contracts more complicated.

If you want to know more about how it works, then traders will be able to access education on how to trade Ripple (XRP) Futures, which has a range of educational resources available, such as contract specifications, trading strategies, and risk management.

This is crucial when volatility is high, and it is necessary to make trades at short time intervals that are leveraged.

Broader market trends influence XRP

XRP is impacted by the broader market. Broad patterns of the cryptocurrency market have an impact on XRP futures trading as well.

Trading patterns can be influenced by several factors, including:

  • Bitcoin's price movements
  • Regulatory developments and news
  • General investor sentiment
  • Broader market liquidity

Hedging or speculation may be at work on the futures market when there is an uptick in activity, as may be the case with growing interest.

Conversely, reduced futures activity may not reflect a negative sentiment, as it may be due to traders reducing leverage or closing out their positions.

Conclusion

The movement of traders' positions, market sentiment, and volatility is useful information for XRP futures.

The open interest, leverage, funding rates, and the trading volume of an asset are useful in clarifying market behavior; however, none of these indicators can predict XRP price movements by itself.

Given the evolving nature of cryptocurrency derivatives markets, it is critical to understand the connection between available relevant spot market conditions and the activity in the futures market.

FAQs

Q1: What is the main difference between XRP spot trading and XRP futures trading? 

Spot trading involves buying or selling actual XRP directly at the current market price. Futures trading involves contracts to speculate on future price movements using leverage, without necessarily owning the underlying asset.

Q2: Does high open interest mean the price of XRP will go up? 

High open interest signifies that more traders and investors are buying and selling interest rates in the marketplace, but it doesn't reveal if traders are entering long (bull) or short (bear) positions.

Q3: How does leverage impact market volatility in XRP futures? 

Using leverage enables traders to make trades larger than they could otherwise with the same amount of money. For the first time, when the market goes simultaneously against these leveraged positions, the simultaneous forced sell-off of these positions, in the opposite direction, can add to a rapid buyer-seller movement and create larger price volatility levels. 

Q4: Why are funding rates important in perpetual futures? 

Funding rates are periodic payments between traders that help keep perpetual futures prices aligned with the spot market price. High positive funding rates indicate strong bullish demand, while negative rates signal bearish sentiment.

data.title: Etsy stock rebounds as Oppenheimer turns bullish: is it a safe buy now?
data.description:
Etsy stock rose by over 3% on Tuesday as analysts started turning bullish on the company. It rose to $76.45, up by nearly 10% from its lowest level this month. But it also remains in a technical correction after falling by 13% from its highest point this year.

Analysts are turning bullish on Etsy stock

Some analysts tracking Etsy have turned bullish on the company, noting that it will be a big beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom. 

In a note released today, Ananya Chetia, an Oppenheimer analyst, said that she expects the stock to jump to $90, suggesting a 21% upside from the current level. She also upgraded the rating from perform to outperform, noting that it will benefit from AI use in virtual shopping. 

Other analysts are bullish on the company. Nikhil Devnani, a Bernstein analyst, upgraded the company from hold to strong buy, while Taylor Conrad, an Argus analyst, hiked the target from $67 to $89. Similarly, analysts from companies like Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, Loop Capital, and Rosenblatt have a bullish outlook for the company. 

Etsy’s business is doing fairly well

Etsy, an online marketplace for handcrafted items, has gone through a rough patch in the past few years as the momentum it experienced during the pandemic. Its revenue growth has slowed, and its relationship with its creators has soured amid the price increases. 

The most recent results showed that it had 87 million active buyers in the second quarter, largely unchanged from the same period last year. Its new buyers were 5 million, up by 4.4% from the same period last year, while the reactivated buyers rose to 7.1 million. 

At the same time, the number of active sellers rose to 5.7 million, up slightly from the same quarter last year. 

With its revenue growth slowing, the management is working to boost its profits. It recently announced that it was laying of 220 employees, equivalent to 12% of its total workforce. This restructuring plan will cost it $35 million. 

Analysts expect that its revenue growth will remain under pressure, especially after the $1.6 billion sale of Depo and Reverb. The average estimate is that its third-quarter revenue will drop by 1.45% to $668 million, with the annual figure falling by 1.16% to $2.85 billion. 

Etsy stock technical analysis

Etsy stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the Etsy share price formed a triple-top pattern at $87 and a neckline at $77.7. A triple-top is one of the most bearish patterns in technical analysis.

It has now slipped below the neckline at $77.77, its neckline and also the 23.6% Fibonacci Retracement level. It is now attempting to bounce back after moving to the 38.2% Fibonacci Retracement level. 

The stock remains below the 50-day moving average and the resistance at $77.77. As such, it is attempting to form a break-and-retest pattern, a common continuation sign. The bearish outlook will remain intact as long as it is below $77.77.
